sections.intro:
Philips Hue & Ambilight Function Specification
1. Document Information
Document Number: SPEC-HUE-AMB-001
Version: V1.0
Date: 2026-09-18
Scope: Philips TV Ambilight and Philips Hue Smart Lighting Integration
Classification: Internal / Confidential
Version History
2. Introduction
sections.2.1:
2.1 Purpose
This document defines the complete functional specification for the Ambilight feature, encompassing hardware layout, color and brightness control, response synchronization mechanisms, and intelligent linkage capabilities with Philips Hue.
sections.2.2:
2.2 Scope
This specification covers all Philips TV models supporting Ambilight and their integration with Philips Hue smart lighting products.
sections.2.3:
2.3 Target Audience
Functional Test Engineers
Product Managers
Hardware Engineers
Firmware Developers
sections.2.4:
2.4 References
IEC 62471: Photobiological Safety of Lamps and Lamp Systems
ENERGY STAR Program Requirements for Televisions
3. Functional Overview
sections.3.1:
3.1 System Architecture
The system comprises the TV-side Ambilight processor, LED strip arrays, Philips Hue Bridge, and Hue lamps. Data flows from the TV video processor to the Ambilight controller, which outputs to the TV LEDs and simultaneously sends sync commands via Wi-Fi to the Hue Bridge, which translates them to Zigbee signals for Hue lamps.
sections.3.2:
3.2 Key Features Summary
Dynamic Color Mapping
Multi-mode Switching
Hue Whole-home Linkage
Audio Synchronization
Ambient Light Adaptation
Voice Control
Shutdown Fade Out
Custom Scenes
sections.3.3:
3.3 Not in Scope
Hue lamp firmware upgrades
Compatibility with non-Philips third-party lamps
HDR tone mapping algorithms
4. Hardware Layout Specification
sections.4.1:
4.1 LED Strip Configuration
Entry Level: Left and right sides only; 24-32 LEDs.
Mid Range: Left, right, and top sides; 40-57 LEDs.
High End: Full four-sided surround; 60+ LEDs.
OLED Flagship: 360-degree surround with pixel-level light sync.
sections.4.2:
4.2 Installation Requirements
Distance from Wall: Recommended 10-25cm (Optimal: 10-15cm).
Wall Color: White, neutral, or light-colored flat surfaces.
Ambient Light: Avoid direct strong light on the LED strip area.
Installation Angle: LED strip to wall angle should be <=30°.
sections.4.3:
4.3 LED Technical Parameters
Color Gamut: Full sRGB coverage.
Brightness Range: 1%-100% adjustable.
Color Temperature (Warm White Mode): 2200K-4500K.
Response Time: < 10ms (Hardware level).
Power Consumption: < 15W in Ambilight mode.
5. Color & Brightness Control Specification
sections.5.1:
5.1 Dynamic Color Extraction
Real-time analysis of edge colors from input video signals (HDMI/Internal).
Processing Frame Rate: >= 30fps input corresponds to >= 30fps light effect update.
Color Mapping Precision: 8-bit per channel (256 levels/channel).
Color Transition Algorithm: Linear interpolation + gradient compensation.
sections.5.2:
5.2 Brightness Control
User Adjustable Levels: Low / Medium / High / Maximum (4 levels).
Auto Brightness: Adaptive based on ambient light sensor (0-1000 lux range).
Max Brightness Limit: User-lockable upper limit to prevent glare at night.
Brightness Adjustment Response Time: < 500ms.
sections.5.3:
5.3 Color Modes
Natural: Faithful reproduction of edge colors with smooth transitions; for daily viewing.
Vivid: Enhanced saturation and brightness; for variety shows/concerts.
Football: Enhanced green pitch tones; dynamic tracking of player movement.
Game: Lowest latency for high-speed画面 changes.
Music: Lights pulse to audio rhythm; supports multiple rhythm algorithms.
Lounge Light: 6500K soft static white light in standby/specific modes to reduce eye strain.
Warm White: Fixed warm white tone with adjustable color temperature.
Custom: User-defined fixed color via color palette.
sections.5.4:
5.4 Saturation Control
Adjustable Levels: 0-100%.
Default Value: 50%.
Adjustment Step: 10%.
sections.5.5:
5.5 Wall Color Compensation
Supported Wall Colors: White / Cream / Light Gray / Dark Gray / Custom.
TV automatically corrects Ambilight output to compensate for wall reflection.
Calibration Precision: CIE ΔE < 5.
sections.5.6:
5.6 Separation Control
Sets the color difference level between left and right lights.
Off: Uniform color presentation.
On: Enhanced stereoscopic effect.
Adjustable Levels: 0-10.
sections.5.7:
5.7 TV Off Fade Out
Option 1: Immediate Switch Off.
Option 2: Fade Out to Off. Adjustable fade time: 3s / 5s / 10s / 30s.
6. Response & Sync Mechanism Specification
sections.6.1:
6.1 End-to-End Latency Requirements
Game Mode: <= 100ms (Must Have)
Movie Mode: <= 200ms (Should Have)
Music Mode: <= 150ms (Should Have)
Natural Mode: <= 200ms (Should Have)
Vivid Mode: <= 150ms (Should Have)
Football Mode: <= 200ms (Should Have)
sections.6.2:
6.2 Responsiveness Adjustment
User-adjustable Ambilight response speed to screen changes (Slider: Slow / Normal / Fast).
Default: Normal.
Fast: Lowest latency but possible slight color jumps.
Slow: Smoothest transition but slightly higher latency.
sections.6.3:
6.3 Transition Smoothness
Color Transition: No stepped abrupt changes, no visible flicker.
High-frequency Flicker Suppression: > 50Hz flicker must be eliminated.
Gradient Color Video Test: Smooth transition to naked eye, no abrupt changes in light curve.
sections.6.4:
6.4 Motion Compensation (MEMC for Ambilight)
Predicts画面 change trends via motion estimation and compensation algorithms.
Adjusts light transitions in advance to avoid disconnection between画面 and lights.
Applicable Scenarios: Game / Football / Vivid modes.
7. Philips Hue Linkage Specification
sections.7.1:
7.1 Connection Protocol
Communication: Wi-Fi (TV side) + Zigbee (Bridge side).
Bridge Compatibility: Philips Hue Bridge 2.0 and above.
Max Supported Hue Lamps: 16 per linkage scene.
Discovery Protocol: mDNS/Bonjour LAN discovery.
Pairing Flow: TV search → User selects Bridge → User confirms pairing → Auto-discover lamps.
sections.7.2:
7.2 Compatible Hue Lamp Types
Color Light: Supported.
Extended Color Light: Supported.
White Ambiance: Supported (Color temperature adjustment only).
White: Not supported for dynamic color linkage.
LightStrip: Supported.
Not Supported: Non-Philips brand lamps, 1st Gen Hue Bridge (v1).
sections.7.3:
7.3 Linkage Modes
Movie Mode Sync: Hue lamps sync with Ambilight colors during movies.
Game Mode Sync: Hue lamps sync with game light effects.
Music Mode Sync: Hue lamps pulse to audio rhythm.
Party Mode: Festive gathering mode; Hue lamps sync with Ambilight for colorful gradient switching.
Custom Scene: User-defined scene rules (e.g., “Dim ceiling lights + Activate surround light effects when watching movies”).
sections.7.4:
7.4 Linkage Latency
TV → Bridge Command Delay: <= 500ms.
Bridge → Hue Lamp Response Delay: <= 300ms.
End-to-End (TV画面 change → Hue lamp color change): <= 1s (Must Have).
sections.7.5:
7.5 Linkage Configuration
Enable/Disable: Settings > Display & Sound > Ambilight > AMBILIGHT EXTENSION > Hue > Enable/Disable.
Configuration: Select and set each Hue lamp to follow Ambilight colors.
View Configuration: View current setup of network, Bridge, and bulbs.
Reset Configuration: Reset current setup.
sections.7.6:
7.6 Hue Linkage Behavior Rules
Network Disconnection: Hue lamps maintain last known state; no flickering or error reporting.
Network Recovery: Auto-reconnect and resume sync within 30s.
Manual Control Conflict: When manually adjusting lights via phone App, TV regains control within 3s (or maintains manual color for 10s before resuming, per product definition).
Multi-Bridge Scenario: Only 1 Bridge supported for simultaneous linkage.
8. Audio Sync Specification
sections.8.1:
8.1 Audio Follow Mode
Lights pulse to audio spectrum rhythm.
Supported Modes: Music / Game.
Rhythm Algorithm Types: Pulse / Gradient / Color Fluctuation (Switchable).
Sensitivity Adjustment: Low / Medium / High.
sections.8.2:
8.2 Philips Wireless Home Speakers Linkage
TV and Philips Wireless Home Speakers connect via Wi-Fi.
Linkage Content: Ambilight light effects change with speaker volume/frequency.
Configuration Path: Settings > Display & Sound > Ambilight > AMBILIGHT EXTENSION > Philips Wireless Home Speakers.
9. Ambient Light Adaptive Specification
sections.9.1:
9.1 Sensor Requirements
Sensor Type: Ambient Light Sensor (ALS).
Detection Range: 0 - 1000 lux.
Sampling Frequency: >= 1Hz.
Calibration: Factory calibration + User manual calibration.
sections.9.2:
9.2 Adaptive Behavior
Daytime (> 300 lux): Enhanced LED brightness and contrast.
Evening (50-300 lux): Medium brightness.
Night (< 50 lux): Auto-reduce brightness by 50%-70% to prevent glare.
Pitch Black (< 5 lux): Minimum brightness mode; only faint halo retained.
sections.9.3:
9.3 Manual Override
User can disable auto-brightness anytime and set fixed brightness levels.
When auto-brightness is off, sensor enters low-power standby mode.
10. Voice Control Specification
sections.10.1:
10.1 Supported Platforms
Google Assistant
Amazon Alexa
Apple HomeKit (Siri)
Samsung SmartThings
sections.10.2:
10.2 Voice Commands
“Hey Siri/Google, Turn on Ambilight Movie Mode”
“Hey Google, set Hue lights to Ambilight sync”
“Alexa, turn off Hue Sync”
“Hey Siri, set Ambilight to Game mode”
sections.10.3:
10.3 Voice Control Response Time
Command to Execution Completion: <= 2s (Must Have).
Command Recognition Accuracy: >= 95% (Standard environment).
11. Power Management Specification
sections.11.1:
11.1 Power Consumption
Ambilight On (Medium Brightness): <= 12W.
Ambilight On (Max Brightness): <= 15W.
Ambilight Off: <= 0.5W (Standby).
Hue Linkage Standby (TV off, Bridge online): <= 1.0W.
sections.11.2:
11.2 Power Saving Modes
Auto Sleep: Ambilight auto-off after 5 minutes of no画面 input.
Timed Off: User-settable timer (30min / 60min / 90min).
Energy Saving Mode: Brightness auto-limited to below 50%.
12. Error Handling & Recovery Specification
sections.12.1:
12.1 Network Failure
TV & Bridge Disconnection: Hue lamps maintain last state; TV Ambilight continues normal operation.
Recovery Time: Auto-reconnect within 30s after network recovery.
User Prompt: App displays offline prompt within 5s.
sections.12.2:
12.2 Device Offline
Single Hue Lamp Power Off: Remaining lamps continue sync; TV side no lag.
Prompt: App displays “Light Offline” notification within 10s.
sections.12.3:
12.3 Bridge Firmware Upgrade
During Upgrade: Linkage function temporarily unavailable.
Post-Upgrade: Auto-restore configuration; no re-pairing needed.
Timeout Handling: If upgrade exceeds 120s without recovery, prompt user for manual check.
sections.12.4:
12.4 Concurrent Trigger Conflict
Priority (High to Low): Game > Football > Movie > Music > Lounge Light > Custom.
Conflict Handling: Higher priority mode overrides lower priority; transition time <= 1s.
13. Performance Requirements Summary
14. Terminology
Ambilight: Philips' proprietary ambient lighting technology that projects colors from the TV screen onto the surrounding wall.
Hue Bridge: The central hub that connects Philips Hue lamps to the TV and network.
Zigbee: Wireless communication protocol used between Hue Bridge and Hue lamps.
MEMC: Motion Estimation and Motion Compensation; algorithm to predict画面 changes for smoother light transitions.
CIE ΔE: Metric for color difference; lower values indicate higher color accuracy.
Lux: Unit of illuminance used to measure ambient light levels.
PWM: Pulse Width Modulation; technique for controlling LED brightness.
mDNS: Multicast DNS; protocol for local network device discovery.
Hue Entertainment Area: Group of Hue lamps configured for synchronized light effects.
Lounge Light: Static ambient light mode for relaxed viewing.
Warm White: Fixed warm color temperature light mode.
Color Light: Hue lamp capable of displaying multiple colors.
Extended Color Light: Hue lamp with wider color gamut and color temperature control.
End-to-End Latency: Total time from画面 change to light effect update.
Fade Out: Gradual dimming of lights when TV is turned off.
Wall Color Compensation: Algorithm to adjust light output based on wall color.
Separation: Control of color difference between left and right Ambilight zones.
ALS: Ambient Light Sensor; detects room lighting for auto-brightness.
Chromasync: Proprietary synchronization protocol between TV and Hue lamps.
